items.headline: NVIDIA chief executive Jensen Huang resigns; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
items.impact: NVIDIA supplies the GPUs behind most large AI training and inference, so a change at the top reaches the whole AI supply chain, from cloud capacity planning to chip roadmaps. The company says operations, customer commitments and its product roadmap continue without interruption, and its next quarterly results are due on 17 November. Not investment advice.

sources.label: NVIDIA Newsroom: NVIDIA Announces CEO Transition
Al Jazeera: Why did Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resign, and who is Colette Kress?

items.what: NVIDIA announced on 12 November 2026 that Jensen Huang has resigned as President, Chief Executive Officer and board member, effective immediately, ending 33 years leading the company he helped found. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress serves as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, Harvey C. Jones becomes the first Chair of the board, and the board has started a search for a permanent successor.

items.headline: Microsoft 365 outage disrupts Outlook, Teams and Copilot in 74 countries
items.impact: Microsoft 365 is core workplace infrastructure for companies and governments, including airlines in India and the health service in the UK, so a day of broken email and collaboration stalls work far beyond IT teams. The incident is a practical reminder to keep tested fallback channels for email and meetings.

sources.label: The Hindu: Microsoft outage live updates, November 13, 2026
The Hindu: Global outage ends as Microsoft restores services, November 14, 2026

items.what: A global Microsoft 365 outage that began on 12 November 2026 disrupted Outlook email, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services, with reports from 74 countries and more than 130,000 reports on outage tracker Downdetector at the peak. Microsoft traced the fault to a technical issue linked to an earlier network capacity upgrade and a recent network change, said there was no evidence of malicious activity, and confirmed services were fully restored on 14 November.

review_queue.headline: FBI says North Korea linked hackers stole over $400 million with a recorded video call scheme
review_queue.held_reason: Sensitive item: a nation state attribution that the accused state publicly denies, with a live geopolitical dispute around it. Held for Thillai's approval under the sensitive items rule; never auto published and never rendered on any page.
review_queue.impact: The scheme targets tech and crypto workers through the meeting tools they trust every day, and the FBI says the group is adding AI generated deepfake videos of well known figures. Verification habits for video calls and for files sent during them now matter as much as email phishing defences.

sources.label: Reuters via GMA News: North Korean hackers steal more than $400 million using video images, FBI says

review_queue.what: In a FLASH alert dated 12 November 2026, the FBI said North Korea linked hackers behind a scheme it calls FaceStealer stole more than $400 million in cryptocurrency over 18 months, using fake video meetings and secretly recorded webcam videos of earlier victims to impersonate people the next target knew. The FBI says it has seized over 900 of those videos, and the US Justice Department obtained court orders covering $1.2 billion linked to a separate exchange theft. North Korea has denied involvement.
